output.title: Which Rx pricing disclaimer to read and when
output.draft_text:
Q: What is the Rx pricing disclaimer I have to read?

A: Before you say any dollar amount, read the pricing disclaimer word for word. Do not shorten it.

Read this disclaimer exactly as written:

"The price I quote is an estimate for a 30-day supply at a preferred retail pharmacy, based on the plan records I can see today. Your actual cost can change if the pharmacy, the days' supply, or your stage of coverage is different. This estimate is not a guarantee of payment."

Source: [approved disclaimer unit ID, e.g., U-RX-EDU-001-09].
author_checklist: Confirm which disclaimer wording is the official script. U-RX-EDU-001-09 (labeled Legal) and U-RX-EDU-002-07 use different wording ('based on' vs. 'using'; 'Your actual cost' vs. 'What you pay'). Legal should confirm the correct version, and the other unit should be retired or corrected.
Confirm the quoted disclaimer text in this draft matches the approved Legal version exactly, word for word.
Consider linking to or reusing the existing approved units instead of publishing a third copy of the disclaimer text. A third copy could drift out of sync.
Confirm the timing rule from U-RX-EDU-001-08 still applies: read the disclaimer before any dollar amount, word for word, without shortening.

Confirm with the pharmacy team whether advocates need guidance when the quote is not for a 30-day supply or not at a preferred retail pharmacy. The approved units do not address this, so do not add guidance unless it is documented.
Decide the owning knowledge base: pharmacy (advocate-facing FAQ) or shared-legal (where the Legal disclaimer is maintained).
